findings.title: KeyError when existing Integration has no `sender` in metadata
findings.body: `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` assumes the `sender` key is always present. It is only set by the installation webhook, and `build_integration` only adds a string `state["sender"]` when one exists. An existing Integration created before this change, or one whose webhook has not arrived or lacked a sender, raises KeyError. The result is a 500 in the install pipeline instead of the friendly error. Use `.get()` chaining and treat a missing value as a mismatch.

findings.title: GitHub user is not validated when no Integration row exists yet
findings.body: When `Integration.DoesNotExist` is raised, the code goes straight to `pipeline.next_step()`. The authenticated GitHub user obtained in OAuthLoginView is never compared with anyone. The sender check only runs for an already existing Integration. If the installation webhook has not been processed yet, or the Integration was removed, anyone can attach another account's `installation_id` to their org. This is the attack the PR is meant to stop.

findings.title: Token exchange and user-info calls can raise and cause a 500
findings.body: `safe_urlopen` is outside the try/except, so a network error or timeout propagates as an unhandled exception. `get_user_info(payload["access_token"])` is also unguarded. A failing GitHub API call, or a response that is not a dict, is not turned into the intended error page. Only the body read and parse are wrapped, so the PR's promise to fail gracefully in these cases is not met.

findings.title: Authorize URL built without URL-encoding parameters
findings.body: `state` and `redirect_uri` are interpolated directly into the query string with no encoding. This works with the current values, but it is fragile. `redirect_uri` is a full URL, so it should go through `urlencode`.

findings.title: test_installation_not_found no longer tests a missing installation
findings.body: The test now submits a hardcoded, different `state` (`ddd023d8...`) and asserts "Invalid installation request.". That error comes from the state/signature mismatch (or a missing pipeline), not from the 404 installation lookup. The original assertion about "The GitHub installation could not be found." was dropped, so the 404 path in `build_integration` is untested. There are also no tests for a failed token exchange, a missing `login`, or a missing `sender` in metadata.
